plugins._comment: Wraps @semantic-release/commit-analyzer (forwarded this preset + releaseRules verbatim) to make the MINOR component an odometer: it climbs to 999, and the release that would become X.1000.0 rolls over to (X+1).0.0 instead. THAT ROLLOVER IS NOW THE ONLY THING THAT BUMPS THE MAJOR — the `breaking` rule below maps to `minor` deliberately. The major has ZERO machine consumers, measured: npmPublish:false, infra/helm was deleted with its sync script (2026-09-02), and the GHCR image is tagged :latest + :sha-<short>, never by version (ghcr-publish.yml:68-70). Every runtime reader takes the whole string (OTel service.version, the diagnostics route, openapi info.version). So spending a major on a breaking change buys nothing and only shortens the odometer, and it had spent two: fix(authz)! took 1.903.12 to 2.0.0 and chore(infra)! took 2.0.5 to 3.0.0, which is why major 2 lasted six releases. DO NOT DELETE THE `breaking` RULE TO GET THIS — SET IT. commit-analyzer falls back to its DEFAULT rules whenever no custom rule matches (index.js:57-66) and default rule 0 is {breaking:true, release:major}, so deleting it yields three different answers by commit type: chore! falls through to major, feat! lands on minor via the feat rule, and fix! lands on PATCH. Verified by execution; pinned by tests/unit/minor-cap.test.ts. See scripts/lib/minor-cap.mjs.

plugins._comment: Assets committed with the release. `infra/helm/inflect/Chart.yaml` was removed from this list on 2026-09-02 together with `infra/helm/` itself — the chart described a Kubernetes deployment that was never provisioned. The paired `@semantic-release/exec` step that ran `scripts/sync-chart-version.mjs` went with it: that script exits non-zero when its regex misses, so leaving it would have failed the PREPARE phase of every release once the file was gone, taking the release pipeline dark on the next push to main.
